title: Bikini Competition Prep Plan
author: Mithosphere
desc:
THE PROGRAM
Delts and the posterior chain are hit twice to build the shoulders, waist, and glutes visual taper that the division requires. Cardio starts low so you have room to scale up later.

Take two rest days, ideally placing one right after your heavy glute day. If you miss a workout, do it the next day and shift your schedule forward—do not double up your sessions.

Keep in mind that contest prep is a temporary extreme—the stage look is not sustainable year-round and is not a health goal. For your safety, you should only run this program alongside a qualified coach and a doctor. This plan covers only the training half of your preparation.

CARDIO
Weekly cardio, start here and only add later:
- INCLINE WALKING - 3 per week, after lifting or on a rest day. 25 min, moderate incline, RPE 5, able to hold a conversation
- ROWING - 1 per week, not the day before a heavy leg day. 15 min steady, RPE 5-6, smooth stroke rate.
- INCLINE WALKING (Supplemental) - 2 per week, added only if progress stalls. Non-consecutive days. 20 min, same incline and RPE as the base sessions
- JUMP ROPE (Optional) - 6-8 min easy, used as a warm-up in place of a walk. Straight into your lifting warm-up.
- SPRINTS - 1  per week, back half only. 6 x 20 sec hard, only if sleep and recovery are holding up. 90 sec easy walk between sprints.

HOW TO PROGRESS
W1-W4: Use weights you can fully control. Add a little weight to the first two exercises of each day only when you hit the top rep ranges. Keep accessory weights unchanged. Hold cardio strictly to the baseline (3 walks + 1 row)—do not add cardio yet, regardless of the scale.
W5-W7: Add one set to the first exercise on Day 1 and Day 4. Push the final set of lateral raises on Day 2 and Day 5 near failure. Only add one extra walk if your weight and mirror progress stall for two consecutive weeks.
W8 DELOAD: Take a mandatory recovery week. Use the same schedule, but drop your total sets by one-third and reduce your weights to 70% of usual loads. Stop all sets well short of failure and drop cardio back to the baseline.
W9-W12: Expect your barbell strength to plateau; focus on form quality instead of chasing heavier weight. Add the second extra walk only if you stall again for two weeks. If sleep, recovery, or your cycle suffers, decrease cardio and increase food immediately.
W13 DELOAD: Repeat the exact same deload structure as Week 8 to clear accumulated fatigue.
W14-W16: Focus on pure consistency using weights you can move beautifully. Drop sprints if they hurt recovery. Your coach completely dictates the final week based on your specific look, division, and physical history.

WARM-UP NOTES
5-8 min cardio + target stretches. Do 2-3 warm-up sets on first exercise. On GLUTE and QUAD days, the warm-up matters more deep into prep.
Keep rest days for resting.
If sick, period stops, or lifting tanks for 3 weeks, drop cardio & add food with your coach/doctor. Discipline won't fix burnout.
